JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a fundamentally sound, large-cap healthcare franchise with strong profitability (21.8% net margin, 25.9% ROE), a diversified Innovative Medicine + MedTech portfolio, and a 50+ year dividend track record. TTM revenue of ~$93.7B and net income of ~$26.9B demonstrate scale and earnings power. However, the trajectory is mixed: Q1 2026 EPS of $2.14 was down sharply from Q1 2025's $4.54 (which likely included a large one-time gain), and sequential QoQ growth is essentially flat (+0.3% revenue, +0.9% EPS). Operating cash flow was weak at $2.51B in Q4 vs $9.17 inB in Q3, suggesting lumpiness. The stock is trading at a P/E of ~26.5x, near the top of its 1-year range (16.8–28.0), and P/B of 6.9x is also elevated vs the 4.7–7.6 range. This means the market is paying a premium for the same earnings power it got more cheaply a year ago. Key headwinds include Stelara loss of exclusivity accelerating through 2026, upcoming LOE for Simponi and Opsumit, talc litigation overhang (75,000+ lawsuits, bankruptcy strategy failed three times), and China VBP pressure in MedTech. On the positive side, the pipeline is active: TALVEY Phase 3 data, IMAAVY achieving its primary endpoint, the $1B Firefly Bio acquisition targeting KRAS-driven tumors, and a $1B Acuvue expansion. The company raised 2026 guidance midpoint to ~$100.8B in sales and FY2026 EPS guidance of $11.45–$11.65. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.51). No clear near-term re-rating catalyst is visible — the next earnings event is Q2 2026, and the stock has already re-rated significantly from its 2025 lows. Net-net: solid defensive franchise but richly valued relative to its own history with patent cliff headwinds, warranting only a mildly positive score.
